A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Dynamically Scaled Activation Steering and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original toxicity-mitigation experiments, capability-retention evaluations, diffusion-model experiments, and extensive ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds AlphaSteer comparisons, quantitative token localization, gate calibration, and detailed latency measurements.

M1.justification: The PCA/logistic gate, per-token interpolation, and joint E2E-DSAS training objectives remain unchanged. Temperature scaling is evaluated diagnostically, not introduced into the deployed method. Algorithm 2's corrected control-activation notation aligns with the loss already specified in v1.

E1.justification: Appendix I.2.1 adds Toxic Spans Detection: 2,000 Civil Comments test posts with human span annotations for quantitative token localization. Existing toxicity, capability-retention, banana-text, and six-concept diffusion coverage is retained.

E2.justification: AlphaSteer joins the toxicity comparisons for all three language models in Table 1 and new Figure 19. Appendix P documents its average-embedding adaptation. CAA, ITI, LinEAS, CAST, and MERA remain in their corresponding comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 adds substantial evaluation protocols: token-label mapping and AUROC/mAP localization metrics; calibration on 600 held-out comments with separate temperature-fitting and testing splits; and prefill/decode profiling across batch sizes and sequence lengths. The existing main toxicity protocol and Table 1's capability budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Previously qualitative token-localization evidence gains a human-annotated quantitative diagnostic, including within-toxic-post evaluation. New calibration and temperature-scaling analyses assess gate confidence, while Appendix A.1 expands runtime analysis across operating conditions. Existing PCA, noise, layer, sample-size, and E2E ablations are retained.

E5.justification: New calibration estimates average over five splits and pool predictions across layers; new latency measurements average 50 iterations after warmup. The retained experiments preserve their four generation seeds, 100-repetition sample-size study, and other previously reported repetition counts.

E6.justification: Existing Table 1 scores are unchanged, but AlphaSteer adds toxicity scores of 11.42%, 6.89%, and 16.32% for the three models. New results include within-toxic localization AUROC of 0.70–0.76, calibration estimates, and detailed latency/throughput measurements. Table 10 and Figure 13 disagree on the third calibration model's identity, limiting attribution of that result.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, steering equations, losses, and Appendix C derivation are retained. Moving the interpolation equation earlier and correcting notation do not introduce new mathematical reasoning. The added calibration and localization metrics are empirical diagnostics.

C1.justification: The introduction and conclusion extend the claimed advantage over conditional-steering methods to AlphaSteer. The central claims about adaptive steering, capability preservation, end-to-end training, and diffusion applicability remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 discusses the offline-training/inference activation mismatch, interprets localization as preferential rather than exact, and argues that source-likeness ranking matters more than probability calibration. It also attributes AlphaSteer's weakness to low-data overfitting. The proposed mask-based localization remedy is removed, while the demonstrated image-localization limitation remains.

D1.justification: v2 adds A100/fp16 and warmup details for profiling, token-annotation processing instructions, calibration procedures, and AlphaSteer's average-embedding adaptation. Algorithm 2's control-activation notation is corrected. Code release remains promised rather than newly supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds AlphaSteer, calibration work by Guo et al., and the Toxic Spans Detection reference. It contrasts DSAS with AlphaSteer's parameterization and removes the earlier description of LinAcT's quantile-based conditional behavior. Other citation-year changes largely refer to the same works.

P1.justification: Section 3.2 now presents the gating equation before its implementation details and clarifies the source/control/target roles. Supporting explanations and appendix subsections are added, with localized language corrections and an Ethics-to-Broader-Impact heading change. The overall narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: The empirical displays expand substantially through latency Tables 4–7, localization/calibration Tables 9–10, reliability Figure 13, and AlphaSteer Figure 19. Figure 1 is revised, Table 1 gains a comparator row, and the layer-ablation table is enlarged. Existing plots and diffusion examples are retained despite renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens support for token selectivity through human annotations, tests practical overhead more thoroughly, and adds a relevant comparator while clarifying the method. These improve an already substantial empirical study without changing its core results. The Table 10/Figure 13 calibration-model mismatch limits confidence in part of the new evidence, but the overall gains remain positive.
